    TransferInteraction(label, *, source, target, state, into=None, amount, flow='', pairing='members', legs=(), fallback=None, guard=None, rate=None, reverse_rate=None, offset=0, boundary='periodic', form='symbolic', schedule='random-sequential', actor='source', partners=None, remove=None, phase=None, settlement=None)

    Bases: Interaction

    Transfer of amounts of states from the members of a source role to the members of a target role.

    A leg moves an amount out of a state of the source member, or out of Source(), into a state of the target member, or into Sink(). The transfer has a first leg, state into into by amount, and any further legs, each (state, into, amount) or (state, into, amount, flow). The amounts of all legs are read before any of them moves, so a leg sees the states as they were before the transfer. A guard skips the transfer where it does not hold.

    The symbolic form reports the amount of every leg as a flow. A leg named by its flow is reported under that name: under the element or group, as <path>.<flow>, when the source and the target are one element or group, since the flow then moves a quantity within it like a flow of its own, and under the interaction, as <label>.<flow>, otherwise, as it is for a subclass that names its roles otherwise. A leg without a name is reported under the interaction as <label>.flow_<index>.

    The form chooses how the transfer lowers:

    • 'symbolic' lowers to TransferLaws between the source and the target of one element, or member i of both groups. The amounts, the guard, and the rates are numbers or functions of the namespace, and the roles are read as namespace.source and namespace.target. With a rate, the amount is the size of a jump at the rate, and with a reverse_rate jumps also move the amounts back from the target to the source at that rate, so a leg from Source() returns its amount to the environment. With an offset, the source is a group and every member transfers along an edge of the group order, to the member offset places along it, which namespace.target reads. Past the ends of a 'fixed' boundary no member is there, and the edge moves nothing. A draw in an amount is one draw per edge, which both of its ends read, so the amounts of a step move in parallel. A leg end '<role>.<state>' names the state of the element or group another role binds, so one transfer moves amounts between several holders, such as the payments of a circuit of sectors, and a subclass that declares parameters reads them in its amounts. A subclass that names its roles otherwise returns their names from _get_role, or the namespaces of the source and the target of every pair from _get_holders.
    • 'agent' lowers to an agent rule, whose amounts and guard are numbers or functions of the source agent, the target agent, and the model view. The pairing 'members' pairs member i of both groups, 'random' pairs every source member with a random target member, 'pairs' draws disjoint random pairs, 'neighbors' pairs every source member with the target members in the cells or nodes around it, 'neighbor-pairs' draws disjoint random pairs of neighbours, every source member in random order taking a random unpaired target member around it, and 'cell' pairs the source and target members that stand in one cell or node. With a fallback group, the members of that group are the targets of a step in which no target member lives. With the pairing 'site' the target role binds a field, and every source member moves its amounts into the site of the field at its cell or node, so a negative amount takes from the site. The functions of this pairing take the cell of the source agent in place of a target agent. With remove, the source or the target member of every pair that transfers is removed, as an agent eaten whole. The named pairings other than 'members' and 'site' are shorthands of a PartnerSpec, which pairs every source member with partners within a radius, by score, or with a fallback. A settlement receives both partners and the amounts of the legs, read once, and changes the states in place of the legs, so one draw credits both ends. A subclass that names its roles otherwise returns their names from _get_role.

    Under the schedule 'random-sequential' the pairs act in random order. Under 'member' every member of the actor role acts in its own activation, together with the rules of its element and the other member interactions, in the order the system lists them: it transfers with its partners, the members of the other role that the pairing 'random', 'neighbors', or 'cell' gives it, or with partners of them drawn at random, and with itself under the pairing 'members' within one group. A leg end of the agent form may name '<reference>.<state>', the state of the member that a reference state of the agent names, such as 'bank.deposits' for the deposits of a customer's bank, declared StateSpec(reference='banks').

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

    		 required
    source Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

    The path of the element or group the amounts leave.

    		 required
    target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

    The path of the element or group the amounts enter, the source again for a transfer within members.

    		 required
    state str | Source

    The name of the state of the source the first leg takes from, or Source() for the environment.

    		 required
    into str | Sink | None

    The name of the state of the target the first leg adds to, Sink() for the environment, or None for state.

    		 None
    amount Amount

    The amount of the first leg, a number or a function.

    		 required
    flow str

    The name the symbolic form reports the first leg under, or the empty string for flow_0.

    		 ''
    pairing str | Pairing

    How members are paired, one of 'members', 'random', 'pairs', 'neighbors', 'neighbor-pairs', 'cell', or 'site', the agent form alone taking the others than 'members', or, in the agent form, a PartnerSpec, or a function pairing(sources, targets, rng, capacity) of the source and target agents that returns their pairs, whose capacity is partners, or 1 without it. Under the schedule 'member' the spec or the function receives the actor alone as its first sequence and the actor's partners are the second items of its pairs.

    		 'members'

    Further legs, each a tuple of a state or Source(), a state, Sink(), or None, an amount, and optionally the name of its flow.

    		 ()
    fallback Annotated[str | None, RoleSpec()]

    The path of the group whose members the agent form pairs with instead of the target members in a step in which no target member lives, or None for no fallback.

    		 None

    A function that returns whether a pair transfers, a condition of the namespace or a boolean of the agents, or None for every pair.

    		 None
    rate Amount | None

    The rate of jumps of the symbolic form, a number or a function of the namespace, or None for a continuous flow.

    		 None
    reverse_rate Amount | None

    The rate of the jumps of the symbolic form that move the amounts back from the target to the source, a number or a function of the namespace, or None for no reverse jumps.

    def transfer(self, source: AgentViewProtocol, target: AgentViewProtocol, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> bool:
    """Move the amounts of every leg from one source agent to one target agent, when the guard holds.

    Args:
        source:
            The agent the amounts leave.

        target:
            The agent the amounts enter.

        model:
            The model view of the rule.

    Returns:
        transferred:
            Whether the guard held, so the amounts moved.

    Raises:
        ValidationError:
            An amount function returns something other than a number.

        SimulationError:
            A leg end names the state of a referenced member, and the reference state names no member.
    """
    if self.guard is not None and not self.guard(source, target, model):
        return False
    legs = self._get_legs()
    amounts = [self._evaluate(amount, source, target, model) for _, _, amount, _ in legs]
    if self.settlement is not None:
        self.settlement(source, target, amounts, model)
        return True
    ends = [
        (
            self._get_end(source, state) if isinstance(state, str) else None,
            self._get_end(target, into) if isinstance(into, str) else None,
        )
        for state, into, _, _ in legs
    ]
    for (taken, given), amount in zip(ends, amounts, strict=True):
        if taken is not None:
            holder, name = taken
            setattr(holder, name, getattr(holder, name) - amount)
        if given is not None:
            holder, name = given
            setattr(holder, name, getattr(holder, name) + amount)
    return True

    TransitionInteraction(label, *, target, state='state', source=0.0, destination=1.0, rate=None, probability=None, condition=None, matrix=None, emission=None, observed=None, over='member', neighborhood=None, after=None, schedule='synchronous', form='symbolic', phase=None)

    Bases: Interaction

    Move of a discrete state of the target from one value to another, or between all its values by a matrix.

    A member whose state holds source moves to destination at a rate, as a jump in continuous time, with a probability in every step of discrete time, or in the step in which a condition holds. With over='neighbors' the rate and the probability are those of one neighbour, written with namespace.target.other for the neighbour: the rates of the neighbours add up, and their probabilities combine as 1 - prod(1 - p), the probability that at least one of them moves the member. With a matrix instead, the state takes the values 0 to n - 1 and steps by the rows of a transition matrix in discrete time, the row of its current value. An emission matrix then draws the observed state of the target from the row that the next value of the state selects, as a hidden Markov source. With a residence time after, a member moves by a probability or a condition only once it has held the source value for after steps, at the earliest at the end of the step that completes them.

    In the 'symbolic' form, every function reads namespace.target, the states and parameters of the target, and the time namespace.t. In the 'agent' form, the target is an agent group and every function takes the agent and the model view, f(agent, model), and returns a number, a truth value, or the rows of a matrix, and a rate r moves an agent with probability 1 - exp(-r) in a step. With over='cell', every member acts on the other members of its cell: it moves each one that holds the source value with the probability, the rate, or the condition f(agent, other, model) of that member agent and the acting member other, each by its own draw.

    The schedule of the agent form orders the members. Under 'synchronous' every member decides from the states at the start of the step, under 'sequential' the members act one after the other in their order, and under 'random-sequential' in a new random order every step, each reading the values the members before it set. Under 'member' every member acts in its own activation, together with the rules of its element and the other member interactions, in the order the system lists them, so one rule of a member runs its movement, transfers, transitions, and life cycle.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    label str

    The label of the interaction, unique among the parts of its system.

    		 required
    target Annotated[str, RoleSpec()]

    The path of the element or group whose state moves.

    		 required
    state str

    The name of the discrete state of the target.

    source SourceValues

    def __init__(
    self,
    label: str,
    *,
    target: Annotated[str, RoleSpec()],
    state: str = 'state',
    source: SourceValues = 0.0,
    destination: float = 1.0,
    rate: Callable[..., SupportsFloat] | None = None,
    probability: Callable[..., SupportsFloat] | None = None,
    condition: Callable[..., object] | None = None,
    matrix: Callable[..., Sequence[Sequence[object]]] | None = None,
    emission: Callable[..., Sequence[Sequence[object]]] | None = None,
    observed: str | None = None,
    over: str = 'member',
    neighborhood: BaseNeighborhood | None = None,
    after: float | None = None,
    schedule: str = 'synchronous',
    form: str = 'symbolic',
    phase: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    super().__init__(label)
    self.target = target
    self.state = state
    self.source = source
    self.destination = destination
    self.rate = rate
    self.probability = probability
    self.condition = condition
    self.matrix = matrix
    self.emission = emission
    self.observed = observed
    self.over = over
    self.neighborhood = neighborhood
    self.after = after
    self.schedule = schedule
    self.form = form
    self.phase = phase

    def move(self, model: ModelViewProtocol) -> None:
    """Move the state of every agent of the target that moves in this step, by the schedule.

    Args:
        model:
            The model view of the interaction.
    """
    agents = list(model.agents(self._get_role('target')))
    if self.schedule == 'synchronous':
        moves = [move for agent in agents for move in self._get_moves(agent, model)]
        self._apply(moves, model)
        return
    order = model.rng.permutation(len(agents)) if self.schedule == 'random-sequential' else range(len(agents))
    for index in order:
        self._move_member(agents[int(index)], model)
